In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DCP is a good marker for the diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinomas, but not as good as α‐FP.
the two markers, α‐FP and DCP, are complementary rather than competitive.

the sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value of DCP are less than that of AFP in Black patients with hepatocellular cancer in South Africa, but that the combination of DCP and AFP is superior to either marker alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DCP and α‐FP can be used in combination for the diagnosis of HCC, with DCP as a confirmatory test for α‐FP.

DCP has no place as an alternative to the established marker α‐FP in the routine diagnosis of hepatocellular cancer in southern African Blacks, but that it can be used in combination with α‐FP to reduce the number of false negatives and to provide a clearer picture of the patient’s disease.
DCP is a good marker of HCC, and is better than α‐FP in certain situations, such as in patients with chronic liver disease and in patients who are positive for HBsAg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DCP and AFP as markers of HCC should be done with caution, and that the combination of both markers is more reliable than the use of a single marker.
we need to continue our work on developing new biomarkers that are better than AFP.
we can’t rely on just one marker to detect hepatocellular carcinoma.
